rationale: Methods, Intervention: "The intervention utilized two commercially available mobile applications—MyFitnessPal and 7-Minute Workout—as digital tools" (step logging and a video circuit workout; no movement-controlled game with a goal or score). No motivation instrument is used either (measures are SF-IPAQ, GHQ-28, single-item life satisfaction and happiness).
doubt: I1: The paper calls the intervention exergaming and virtual reality but describes only fitness-tracking and workout apps; does a label the authors apply count when the described intervention does not meet the I1 definition?

criterion: E6: No motivation results by arm
rationale: Questionnaires outcomes: "The RAI score is 15.79±3.80" is one pooled value for the VR program; BREQ-2 results are given for no control-arm figure or table (Table III covers FMA-UE, MMT and BI only). BREQ-2 meets I5 but I6 fails.
doubt: I6: BREQ-2 is reported as a single RAI value described as the patients' motivation towards VR; the text does not say whether the control group completed it. Does a missing control result count as absent or only unreported?

rationale: Abstract: "Outcome measures included concentration, hand and foot reaction time, flexibility, and multidirectional balance." No motivation instrument appears in the methods or results.
Outcome measures: outcomes were VAS, SF-MPQ, ODI, PFDI-20, PGQ and SSQ; none measures exercise motivation ("Pain intensity was the primary outcome measured using the VAS").
doubt: I1: The VR arm uses Meta Quest 2 low-back-pain modules with movement-driven tasks; unclear whether this meets the exergame definition. Not needed for the decision because E5 applies.

rationale: Methods: "Participants were then instructed to continue the 10-minute intervention daily for 7 consecutive days independently"; the paper reports a "1-week period". Intrinsic Motivation Inventory was used, but the exergame arm was scheduled for one week.
